slides.heading: The Rise of Humanoid Robots
slides.body: How machines shaped like us are stepping into our world — and what comes next

slides.heading: Why Human Shape?
slides.body: Humanoid robots are built to work in spaces designed for people — doorways, staircases, and tools built for human hands. A human-shaped body lets them slot into existing environments without expensive retrofits.

slides.heading: Who's Building Them?
slides.body: Tesla's Optimus, Figure AI, Boston Dynamics' Atlas, and Agility Robotics' Digit are leading the race. Dozens of startups and major manufacturers are pouring billions into the space, signaling a genuine industry shift.

slides.heading: From Factory Floor to Your Home
slides.body: The first deployments are in warehouses and manufacturing lines, handling repetitive tasks like sorting and assembly. The long-term vision is a general-purpose helper that can cook, clean, and assist with elder care.

slides.heading: The AI Brain Behind the Body
slides.body: Modern humanoids are powered by foundation models trained on vast human video data. This lets them learn new tasks from just a few demonstrations rather than requiring months of manual programming.

slides.heading: Key Engineering Challenges
slides.body: Balance, dexterity, and energy efficiency remain hard problems. A robot that can walk across uneven terrain, open a bottle, and run for eight hours on a single charge still pushes the edge of what's possible.

slides.heading: Cost: The Final Barrier
slides.body: Early units cost $100,000–$200,000 each. Manufacturers are targeting the $20,000–$30,000 range by the end of the decade through mass production and cheaper actuators — close to the price of a car.

slides.heading: Jobs, Safety & Ethics
slides.body: Economists debate whether humanoid robots will eliminate jobs or create new ones. Safety certification, liability when a robot injures someone, and data privacy in home environments are urgent regulatory questions with no settled answers yet.

slides.heading: The Next Three Years
slides.body: Expect tens of thousands of units deployed in industrial settings by 2027, followed by pilot programs in hospitality and healthcare. Consumer models are still further out, but the roadmap is accelerating faster than most predicted.

slides.heading: The Robot Era Is Here
slides.body: Humanoid robots are no longer science fiction. Understanding their capabilities — and limits — puts you ahead of one of the defining technology shifts of the next decade.
